sections.COMMENTS:
This Composite Source straddles the region from the cities of Macerata (to the northwest) toward Teramo (to the southeast) and is the southernmost part of the Umbro-Marche Apennines outer onshore thrust. This front is the E- to NE-verging fault system at the eastern border of the Northern Apennines chain, parallel to the Marche coast.
Historical and instrumental catalogues (ISIDe Working Group, 2007; Guidoboni et al., 2019; Rovida et al., 2021) show a few key earthquakes in this region, including (from north to south) the 1480 (Me 5.4) Marche Meridionali, and the 3 October 1943 (Mw 5.7) Ascolano events. The area also shows a sparse intermediate (4.5 < Mw < 5.0) seismicity.
The tectonic activity of this region is still not clearly documented but a plausible interpretation is that it is the southern sector of the Northern Marche blind thrust. Subsurface data (Bally et al., 1986; Calamita et al., 1991; Scisciani et al., 2002; Bigi et al., 2013) have well imaged the thrust plane that affects the whole Meso-Cenozoic succession, in particular to the south of the area. Various evidence suggest that the region is undergoing NE-SW trending compression, including earthquake focal mechanisms all along the outer onshore front (Frepoli and Amato, 1997; Pondrelli et al., 2002), while borehole breakout data (Mariucci and Montone, 2020) illustrated a NW-SE trending minimum stress axis.

pictures.t: Map of hypocenter distribution with depth
pictures.c: Map showing in the inner Marche region deep crustal seismicity with depth ranging between 14 and 35 km. Shallower seismicity associated with compressional events is recorded in the coastal and off-shore zones (from Chiarabba et al. [2005]).

Depth distribution of deep crustal and subcrustal earthquakes and geometry of the Adria lithosphere flexured beneath the Apennines. The lowermost profile cuts across the Marche region (from Chiarabba et al. [2005]).

pictures.t: Map of depth of seismogenic layer in Italy
pictures.c: A map of the depth of the bottom of the seismogenic layer in the Marche region shows progressively deeper earthquakes moving westward from the axis of the Northern Apennines. Shallower depths are again found along the Adriatic coastline (from Chiarabba et al. [2005]).

The Stress Map of Italy shows a NE-SW compressional tectonic regime acting in the coastal Marche region. The directions of Shmin follow the trend of the Northern Apennines fronts from the southern Marche to the Po Plain (from Montone et al. [2004], modified).

pictures.t: Map and section of Sn attenuation zone in Italy
pictures.c: Map and cross-sections showing Sn attenuation zone in Italy. The cross-section perpendicular to the Northern Apennines suggests the presence of a westward dipping mantle slab in this area (from Mele et al. [1997]).

pictures.t: Profile of seismic activity in the Northern Marche
pictures.c: The profile highlights the earthquake activity of the central-northern Apennines along the Coastal Thrust Front (CTF) and the occurrence of a strip of deeper events to the southwest, possibly related to the deeper portion of the same thrust (from Burrato et al. [2004]).

pictures.t: Map showing Moho depths along the CROP3 profile
pictures.c: Moho depths estimated along the CROP03 profile. The doubling of the Moho in the Val Tiberina and the westward deepening of the Adriatic Moho seen in the Marche region suggest the  existence of a slab of Adriatic lithosphere (from Mele and Sandvol [2003]).
Detail of a regional cross section showing the hypothesized location of the source of the 1943 Offida earthquake (from Bally et al. [1986], modified).

The main anticlines develop at the base of Triassic level involving the entire Meso-Cenozoic succession. The buried thrust located east of Montagna dei Fiori is proposed as the source of the Offida earthquake (from Calamita et al. [1991], modified).

pictures.t: Seismotectonic zoning of the Central Apennines
pictures.c: The 1943 Offida earthquake is located in the zone B (Foothill seismotectonic zone) where a change of the tectonic regime with depth is expected (contraction in the lower crust and extension in the upper crust) (from Lavecchia et al. [2003]).

pictures.t: Relationship between recent seismicity and thrust faults
pictures.c: Recent seismicity projected on geological cross sections by Lavecchia et al. [2003]. Notice the difference in depth between the Porto San Giorgio sequence, occurring in the uppermost 10 km of the crust, and the Faenza sequence, occurring at 10-12 km and 15-20 km depth.

pictures.t: Structural map of the central Adriatic sea
pictures.c: Generalized structural map of the central Adriatic sea and cross-section of the external thrust fronts (from Scrocca [2006]).

pictures.t: Regional cross-sections across the Po Plain and the northern Adriatic Sea
pictures.c: Interpreted regional seismic reflection profiles straddling the full extents of the Adriatic basin, including the Po Plain and the adjacent Northern Apennines (to the west), Southern Alps (to the north), and Dinarides (to the east) (from Fantoni and Franciosi [2009]).
